newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shinhan foreign bid/share ratio at 45.02.
newsitem.headline: Shinhan foreign bid/share ratio at 45.02.

text.p: The bid-to-share ratio for South Korea's Shinhan Bank shares newly available to foreigners reached 45.02 at pre-opening bidding on Friday, a Securities Supervisory Board official said.

An additional 3.13 million, or 2.54 percent, of Shinhan's outstanding shares became newly available to foreign investors on Friday. The new shares were on top of the 23 percent ceiling in effect for most stocks.
Authorities approved the extra shares because foreigners have had a 2.54 percent stake in the bank since its foundation.
On May 2, the ceiling on foreign ownership in most South Korean stocks was raised to 23 percent of individual companies from the previous 20 percent.
The ceiling is set at 18 percent for two strategically important companies, Pohang Iron and Steel Co and Korea Electric Power Corp.
Shinhan Bank shares were trading flat at 10,300 won by the close of the morning session, with a total of 3.25 million shares changing hands.
